title: Block & file storage
oneLiner: Pick the shape: EBS is a disk for one instance in one AZ, EFS is a Linux share across AZs, and FSx is the file system you already know (Windows, Lustre, NetApp, ZFS). gp3 sets IOPS without buying space.

notes.html: First decide the shape: a disk for one instance (block), a folder many machines share (file), or objects you fetch by key (S3). Then pick the product.

notes.caption: Pick the shape first, then the product

items: "More IOPS without paying for more space" → gp3. With gp2 you'd have to grow the volume.
gp3's maximum was raised to 80,000 IOPS in 2025. Learn 16,000 for the exam, and pick io2 when a question needs more than that.
Multi-Attach needs a cluster-aware file system; plain ext4/xfs will corrupt.

head: Snapshot feature
What it does
rows: Only changed blocks; stored in S3 behind the scenes
DR and migration; encryption can be added during the copy
About 75% cheaper storage; 24-72 h to restore
Recover snapshots or AMIs deleted by mistake within a retention period
No first-read slowness on new volumes (extra cost)

HPC, ML training, "process S3 data fast"

NFS + SMB + iSCSI, or migrating from NetApp

items: Windows file shares → never EFS (Linux/NFS only).
"Lowest latency shared storage for a few Linux HPC nodes reading S3" → Lustre, not EFS.

Note

questions.q: A database on EBS gp2 needs 12,000 IOPS but only 500 GB of space. The team wants the cheapest option that meets the IOPS without buying extra space. What should they do?

options.t: Grow the gp2 volume to 4,000 GB
options.why: gp2 IOPS are tied to size (3/GB), so you'd pay for space you don't need.

options.t: Change to gp3 and provision 12,000 IOPS
options.why: Right. gp3 sets IOPS independently of size.
Works but costs more than gp3 at this level.
HDD; can't deliver this IOPS and can't boot.

questions.q: A transactional database needs 60,000 sustained IOPS with sub-millisecond latency. Which volume type should be used on the exam?

options.why: On the exam gp3 tops out at 16,000 IOPS (raised in 2025, but learn 16,000).
Right. Built for high, sustained IOPS.

questions.q: A Windows application on several EC2 instances needs a shared file system using SMB with Active Directory permissions. What should be used?

options.why: EFS is NFS for Linux only.

options.t: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

options.why: Block storage, needs a cluster file system, not SMB.
For on-prem access to S3, not EC2 shared drives.

questions.q: An ML team trains on a 200 TB dataset in S3 and needs a high-performance file system for a two-day training job. Cost matters. What should they use?

options.t: FSx for Lustre, scratch deployment, linked to the S3 bucket
options.why: Right. Fast, temporary, reads S3 directly.
Much slower for HPC and costlier for this burst.
Works, but scratch is cheaper for a short job.

questions.q: A company is moving from on-premises NetApp storage that serves NFS and SMB clients and some iSCSI LUNs. They want the least change. What should they use?

options.why: A hybrid bridge, not a replacement for the array.

questions.q: A company migrates a ZFS file server and needs high availability across AZs. Which statement is true?

options.t: FSx for OpenZFS is single-AZ only, so use EFS
options.why: Out of date. OpenZFS supports Multi-AZ.

options.t: FSx for OpenZFS supports Multi-AZ deployments
ZFS must run on EC2 with EBS

questions.q: Web servers in three AZs need the same Linux file share for uploaded content. Throughput needs swing a lot during the day. What should be used?

options.why: gp3 can't multi-attach, and EBS is one AZ.
Right. Shared across AZs, throughput scales with demand.
SMB, and these are Linux servers.

questions.q: A cluster-aware application needs several EC2 instances in one AZ to write to the same block volume at the same time. What should be used?

options.why: Right. Same AZ, up to 16 instances, cluster-aware FS required.
That's file storage; the question asks for a shared block volume.

questions.q: A cache layer needs the highest possible random I/O. Data is copied from S3 at boot and can be lost. What is the cheapest, fastest option?

options.why: Fast but pays for durability you don't need.
Right. Highest IOPS, included with the instance, data is temporary.

questions.q: An instance was terminated and its root volume data is gone. Next time the team wants the root volume kept. What should they set?

options.why: Hibernation is for stop/start, not termination.

options.t: Set DeleteOnTermination to false for the root volume

questions.q: An admin deleted important EBS snapshots by mistake. The company wants to be able to recover such deletions for 14 days with the least effort. What should they use?

options.t: Recycle Bin retention rule for snapshots

options.why: Prevents deletes entirely; not a recovery feature.

questions.q: Snapshots must be kept 7 years for compliance and are almost never restored. What cuts their storage cost the most?

options.t: Move them to the EBS Snapshot Archive tier
options.why: Right. ~75% cheaper; 24-72 h restore is fine here.

questions.q: An EBS volume in us-east-1a must be used by an instance in us-east-1b. What should be done?

options.why: EBS volumes are locked to their AZ.

options.t: Snapshot it and create a new volume from the snapshot in us-east-1b

questions.q: On-premises applications need NFS access to files that are stored as objects in S3, with a local cache for frequently used files. What should be used?

options.why: Moves data; doesn't present a file share.
In AWS, not a local cache.

questions.q: A company wants to stop using physical tapes but keep its existing backup software that writes to tape libraries. What should it use?

options.why: Right. Virtual tape library, tapes stored in S3/Glacier.
One-off transfer, not a tape replacement.

questions.q: A new customer in 2026 wants a low-latency on-premises cache for an FSx for Windows file share. What should the architect keep in mind?

options.t: FSx File Gateway is the standard answer and available to everyone
options.why: It's no longer available to new customers (since late 2024).

options.t: FSx File Gateway isn't offered to new customers; consider alternatives such as FSx for Windows over DX/VPN or third-party caching
options.why: Right. Older exam questions may still list it.

questions.q: A company must copy 80 TB from an on-prem NFS server to EFS over a 10 Gbps Direct Connect link, with integrity checks and a nightly sync after that. What should they use?

options.why: Offline; the network is good enough, and nightly syncs need an online tool.
Right. Online, scheduled, verified transfers to EFS.
For S3 uploads over the internet.
Works but you build and run everything.

questions.q: Partners must upload files over SFTP straight into an S3 bucket, without managing servers. What should be used?

options.why: Not an SFTP endpoint for partners.

questions.q: Which TWO EBS volume types can't be used as boot volumes?
A company needs to move 3 PB from a remote site with a 100 Mbps link within a few weeks. What should they use?

options.why: 100 Mbps would take years for 3 PB.
Right. Offline transfer at petabyte scale.
Takes weeks to set up and the site link is the limit.
